earlier_scan.source_named: Christmas, J. Elisabeth & Raymond B. Christmas. 1975. SIL descriptive materials on Kupia (phonology/clause patterns); not found online.

sources.citation: Christmas, R. B. & J. E. Christmas. 1973. Clause patterns in Kupia. In R. L. Trail (ed.), Patterns in clause, sentence, and discourse in selected languages of India and Nepal, Part II: Clause, 257-343. Norman: SIL of the University of Oklahoma. (SIL archive 8946, PDF 26469 via the Internet Archive; image-only scan, pp. 257-262 scanned)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number 3254.183)
sources.note: Introduction repeats the phoneme chart (p. 258: nasalization and length phonemic); no stress statement in the introductory/script section. Body is tagmemic clause analysis.

sources.citation: Christmas, R. B. & J. E. Christmas. 1973. Sentence patterns in Kupia. In R. L. Trail (ed.), Patterns in clause, sentence, and discourse in selected languages of India and Nepal, Part I: Sentence and discourse, 125-195. Norman: SIL of the University of Oklahoma. (ERIC ED087206)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only a phoneme chart (Figure 1, p. 126) with footnotes that nasalization and vowel length are phonemic; no mention of stress or accent anywhere in the Kupia paper (a full-text search for stress/accent full text: only 'intonation' for interrogatives).

sources.citation: Dash, Biswanandan & Subrat Kalyan Pattanayak. 2023. Numeral to numeral of Balmiki and Kupia: a morphological comparison. Journal of Language 5(2). doi:10.30743/jol.v5i2.7707
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Numeral morphology only; no stress statement. Reference list names the PLSI 'Kupiya' chapters (Telugu 2015, English 2019) and Shirtz 2017 (U Oregon diss. using Kupia data).

sources.citation: Mohanty, Panchanan. 2016. A pilot study of Walmiki and its present status (keynote). In N. Ostler & P. Mohanty (eds.), Language colonization and endangerment: Proceedings of FEL XX, x-xiv. Hungerford: Foundation for Endangered Languages.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Numerals, kinship and body-part vocabulary of Walmiki (Koraput); no phonology, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Kaplan, Abby. 2010. Phonology shaped by phonetics: the case of intervocalic lenition. PhD dissertation, UC Santa Cruz (ROA-1077).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lenition-survey appendix row 'Kupia (Sujanakota)': labial spirantization, retroflex flapping; nothing on stress placement.

sources.citation: Blumenfeld, Lev. 2006. Constraints on phonological interactions. PhD dissertation, Stanford University (ROA-877).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Second-hand list of stress-sensitive weakening (ex. 6): 'Kupia — spirantiz., flapping — V__unstrV — Christmas & id. 1975'. No placement rule.

sources.citation: Kirchner, Robert. 1998. An effort-based approach to consonant lenition. PhD dissertation, UCLA (ROA-276; published Routledge 2001).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Second-hand from Christmas & Christmas 1975: Table 1-6 (p. 11) 'Kupia — Christmas & Christmas 1975 — spirantization, flapping /V__V[-stress]'; Table 4-3 (p. 103) 'ʈ→ɽ /V__V unstressed (obligatory), ɖ→ɽ /V__V unstressed (optional)'; Table 4-5 (p. 107) 'p→ɸ /V_V unstressed'. Confirms Kupia has word stress relevant to allophony but gives no placement rule.

sources.citation: Trail, Ronald L. (ed.) 1973. Patterns in clause, sentence, and discourse in selected languages of India and Nepal, Part IV: Word lists. Norman: SIL of the University of Oklahoma. (Kupia word list by R. B. & J. E. Christmas.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The Kupia word list may be transcribed with stress marks and carry a phonological key; open at SIL archive entry 8617 (sil.

sources.access_detail: HathiTrust digitized, search-only (in copyright); interlibrary loan (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: The only dedicated phonology of Kupia; Kirchner 1998 and Blumenfeld 2006 cite it for stress-conditioned lenition, so it must contain a stress/suprasegmental section with the placement statement. HathiTrust has it digitized (mdp.39015024202825, search-only) — obtainable via ILL/HathiTrust ETAS or a Michigan scan; SIL archive 37223 lists it 'Not Available Online' (could be requested from SIL L&C Archives).
